prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t one universal “best” — the right company for you depends on your neighborhood, your home size, budget, desired equipment brand/efficiency, and the installer’s workmanship. I can, however, point you to a few reputable options that serve Atlanta and give you a checklist and practical steps to pick the best installer for your job.

A few well-known providers that serve the Atlanta area (good starting points)
- Coolray — large regional company, lots of reviews, financing options.
- One Hour Heating & Air / Benjamin Franklin (franchises) — strong guarantees on arrival times and service.
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (also does HVAC) — big company with wide service network.
- Aire Serv — national franchise with local technicians.
- Local independent shops — often deliver better price and personalized service; search Google for “HVAC replacement [your ZIP]” and look for 4+ star businesses with detailed recent reviews.

How to choose the best company
1. Get at least 3 written estimates. Compare apples-to-apples: same system size (tons), same SEER rating, same brand/model if possible, and exactly what’s included (permit, ductwork, new condenser, coil, thermostat, disposal).
2. Make sure they perform a Manual J load calculation (not “rule of thumb”) so the system is sized correctly.
3. Check credentials: ask for local license (or permit history), proof of insurance, and NATE-certified technicians if possible.
4. Read recent reviews on Google, Yelp, and the Better Business Bureau; look for repeat mentions of workmanship and honoring warranties.
5. Ask about warranties: equipment warranty (manufacturer) and labor/installation warranty (at least 1 year; longer is better).
6. Ask whether they’ll inspect/repair ducts and airflow (poor ductwork or low airflow ruins efficiency).
7. Get the timeline and cleanup policy in writing; confirm who pulls necessary permits.

What to ask in your estimate (quick checklist)
- Will you get a Manual J (load) and Manual S (equipment selection)?
- SEER rating and model numbers of the proposed equipment.
- Exactly what’s included: condenser, coil, line set, thermostat, start-up, permit fees.
- Labor warranty length and what it covers.
- Financing options, rebates, and potential utility incentives.
- Estimated total price and payment schedule.

Ballpark cost (Atlanta area)
- Full central AC replacement typically runs roughly $3,500–$8,500 for most homes (basic to mid-efficiency units). High-efficiency systems or complex installs (ductwork, two-story homes, line-set replacement, additional permitting) can push $8,000–$12,000+.
- These are rough ranges — get local quotes for specifics.

Brands to consider
- Trane, Carrier, Lennox, Rheem, Goodman — each has tradeoffs of price, reliability, and efficiency. Good installation matters more than brand in many cases.

Next step I can help with
- If you give your ZIP code or neighborhood and any preferences (brand, budget, timeframe), I can find top-rated installers near you and draft a short list and message you can send to them for a quote.
- Or I can draft an email/script you can use to request comparable quotes from three companies.
